mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but SPX returns are negative over 60 days in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 8% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment falls below 8% but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS is low and UNRATE high but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS during a tightening cycle increases borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises above 4% but SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production signals economic strength, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production rises but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing nonfarm employment indicates a strong job market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Nonfarm employment increases but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High GDP and low unemployment indicate strong economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDP is high and UNRATE low but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
